title: Tier Path Prioritizer: quota-aware routing and controlled demotion for free/paid/enterprise
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Implement a Tier Path Prioritizer that routes requests for free, paid, and enterprise plans using a scored path model. The prioritizer will: 1) compute a dynamic path score per request (region affinity, plan tier, SLA class, observed latency, token budget left), 2) perform quota-aware admission and proportional spillover when a tier is constrained, and 3) trigger controlled demotion to cheaper model variants or regional fallbacks rather than hard rejects. The goal is predictable tail latency for enterprise customers while preserving capacity for paid tiers and providing graceful degraded service for free-tier users. This ticket covers design, implementation, rollout flags, unit/integration tests, and dashboards for validating behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Path scorer computes consistent priority values across services and returns routing decision within 2ms median
When paid-tier quota is exhausted, decisions spill proportionally to enterprise-only warm pool, regionally preferring eu/us per tenant settings
Free-tier requests receive a controlled demotion path to quantized-smaller model variants with a 90th percentile latency under 600ms in steady state
Fallback triggers a model-variant downgrade (e.g., gpt-small-q8) with no customer-visible 5xx errors; 95% of downgraded requests produce acceptable output per eval set
Feature flag controls: off (legacy routing), staged (canary 5% tenants), on (global)
Observability: dashboards for path decisions, per-tier acceptance rate, demotion frequency, and end-to-end latency by region
steps: Design path scoring formula and config knobs (weighting for quota pressure, region affinity, SLA multipliers)
Implement admission controller library as a thin service used by routing proxy and console simulator
Add model-variant catalog mapping and demotion rules in config store
Wire telemetry (decision logs) to existing tracing and metrics pipelines with sample keys for PII safety
Create harness for load-test scenarios: quota depletion, regional outage, and burst windows
Run 1% canary with synthetic tenants, iterate on thresholds, expand to 5%/20%/100% rollout
